question.prompt:
Each of the three circles in the adjoining figure is externally tangent to the other two, and each side of the triangle is tangent to two of the circles. If each circle has radius three, then the perimeter of the triangle is

[Figure 1](figures/1977_AMC_12_Q15_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Joining the circle centers turns the tangency conditions into known lengths. Let the upper center be \(O_1\), and the lower centers be \(O_2,O_3\). External tangency gives \(O_1O_2=O_2O_3=O_3O_1=6\), so their triangle is equilateral.

Each side of the enclosing triangle is parallel to the segment joining the two centers nearest that side. Indeed, those centers lie on the same side of the tangent line, both at perpendicular distance 3 from it. Thus the enclosing triangle also has three \(60^\circ\) angles and is equilateral.

Call its bottom vertices \(A,B\), and let \(P,Q\) be the points where the lower left and lower right circles touch \(AB\), respectively. The equal perpendicular radii \(O_2P,O_3Q\) show that \(PQ=O_2O_3=6\).

The lower left circle touches both sides meeting at \(A\). The line from \(A\) to its center bisects the angle between these tangents, so \(\angle O_2AP=30^\circ\). Also, a radius to a tangent is perpendicular to it. Therefore \(AO_2P\) is a right triangle with \(O_2P=3\). The side opposite \(30^\circ\) is half the hypotenuse, giving \(AO_2=6\), and the Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
AP=\sqrt{6^2-3^2}=3\sqrt3.
\]
The same argument at \(B\) gives \(QB=3\sqrt3\). Consequently,
\[
AB=AP+PQ+QB=6+6\sqrt3.
\]
The perimeter is \(3AB=\boxed{18+18\sqrt3}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Join the centers and split one side
Use 30° right triangles at the vertices
